gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: When people applying to medical school ask her for advice, she wants to shake them and yell "Don't do it!" (But she never does.) How did she get into this fix?
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 申请医学院的人向她请教时，她真想抓住他们摇晃，大喊：‘千万别读！’（但她从来没有真的这样做。）她怎么会陷入这种困境？

alignedParts.en: When people applying to medical school ask her for advice, she wants to shake them and yell "Don't do it!"
alignedParts.cn: 申请医学院的人向她请教时，她真想抓住他们摇晃，大喊：‘千万别读！’

alignedParts.en: (But she never does.) How did she get into this fix?
alignedParts.cn: （但她从来没有真的这样做。）她怎么会陷入这种困境？

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: In high school she already wanted to be a doctor.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 高中时，她就想当医生。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: And she is so ambitious and determined that she overcame every obstacle along the way — including, unfortunately, not liking it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 她抱负远大、意志坚定，克服了一路上的所有障碍——不幸的是，也包括“不喜欢这份工作”这个障碍。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Now she has a life chosen for her by a high-school kid.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 现在，她过着一个高中生替她选定的人生。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: When you're young, you're given the impression that you'll get enough information to make each choice before you need to make it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 年轻时，你得到的印象是：在必须做出每个选择之前，都会获得足够的信息。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: But this is certainly not so with work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 但选择工作时，显然不是这样。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: When you're deciding what to do, you have to operate on ridiculously incomplete information.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 决定做什么时，你掌握的信息少得荒唐。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Even in college you get little idea what various types of work are like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 即使在大学，你对各种工作的实际样子仍然知之甚少。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: At best you may have a couple internships, but not all jobs offer internships, and those that do don't teach you much more about the work than being a batboy teaches you about playing baseball.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 最好的情况，也不过是有几次实习；但并非所有工作都有实习，即使有，你对真正工作的了解，也未必比一个球童对打棒球的了解多多少。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: In the design of lives, as in the design of most other things, you get better results if you use flexible media.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 设计人生和设计大多数其他东西一样，采用灵活的方式，往往能得到更好的结果。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: So unless you're fairly sure what you want to do, your best bet may be to choose a type of work that could turn into either an organic or two-job career.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 所以，除非你相当确定自己想做什么，否则最好的选择，可能是一份既能走自然发展路线、又能走双工作路线的工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: That was probably part of the reason I chose computers.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 这大概也是我选择计算机的一部分原因。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: You can be a professor, or make a lot of money, or morph it into any number of other kinds of work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 你可以当教授，也可以赚很多钱，还可以转向许多其他类型的工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: It's also wise, early on, to seek jobs that let you do many different things, so you can learn faster what various kinds of work are like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 刚开始时，寻找能让你接触多种任务的工作也很明智，这样能更快了解不同工作的实际样子。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Conversely, the extreme version of the two-job route is dangerous because it teaches you so little about what you like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 相反，双工作路线的极端版本很危险，因为它几乎不能帮助你认识自己喜欢什么。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: If you work hard at being a bond trader for ten years, thinking that you'll quit and write novels when you have enough money, what happens when you quit and then discover that you don't actually like writing novels?
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 如果你努力做了十年债券交易员，想着赚够钱就辞职写小说，可辞职后才发现自己其实不喜欢写小说，那怎么办？

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Most people would say, I'd take that problem.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 大多数人会说：“这种烦恼我愿意要。”

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Give me a million dollars and I'll figure out what to do.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 给我一百万美元，我自会想清楚做什么。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: But it's harder than it looks.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 但这比看起来更难。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Constraints give your life shape.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 约束给生活塑造了形状。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Remove them and most people have no idea what to do: look at what happens to those who win lotteries or inherit money.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 去掉约束，大多数人就不知道该做什么了；看看中彩票或继承财产的人会怎样就知道。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Much as everyone thinks they want financial security, the happiest people are not those who have it, but those who like what they do.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 尽管人人都觉得自己想要经济保障，最快乐的人却不是那些已经拥有经济保障的人，而是喜欢自己所做之事的人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: So a plan that promises freedom at the expense of knowing what to do with it may not be as good as it seems.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 因此，一个承诺带来自由、却让你无法弄清该如何使用自由的计划，可能没有看上去那么好。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Whichever route you take, expect a struggle.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 不论选择哪条路线，都要准备好经历一番挣扎。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Finding work you love is very difficult.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 找到自己热爱的工作非常困难。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Most people fail.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 大多数人都失败了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Even if you succeed, it's rare to be free to work on what you want till your thirties or forties.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 即使成功，通常也要等到三四十岁，才能自由地做自己想做的工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: But if you have the destination in sight you'll be more likely to arrive at it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 但只要看得见目的地，你就更有可能到达。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: If you know you can love work, you're in the home stretch, and if you know what work you love, you're practically there.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 如果你知道自己能够热爱工作，就已经进入最后冲刺；如果知道自己热爱的是哪种工作，就几乎已经到达终点了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 1 ] Currently we do the opposite: when we make kids do boring work, like arithmetic drills, instead of admitting frankly that it's boring, we try to disguise it with superficial decorations.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [1]目前我们却反其道而行之：让孩子做枯燥的任务，比如算术练习时，我们不坦率承认它很无聊，而是用表面的装饰来掩盖。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 2 ] One father told me about a related phenomenon: he found himself concealing from his family how much he liked his work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [2]一位父亲告诉我一个相关现象：他发现自己在向家人隐瞒，他有多喜欢自己的工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: When he wanted to go to work on a saturday, he found it easier to say that it was because he "had to" for some reason, rather than admitting he preferred to work than stay home with them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 周六想去工作时，他觉得找个理由说自己“不得不去”，比承认自己更愿意工作、而不是待在家里陪他们，要容易一些。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 3 ] Something similar happens with suburbs.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [3]郊区也存在类似的情况。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Parents move to suburbs to raise their kids in a safe environment, but suburbs are so dull and artificial that by the time they're fifteen the kids are convinced the whole world is boring.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 父母搬到郊区，是为了让孩子在安全的环境中长大；但郊区如此单调、如此人工化，以至于孩子到了十五岁，就确信整个世界都很无聊。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 4 ] I'm not saying friends should be the only audience for your work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [4]我不是说，朋友应该是你作品唯一的受众。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: The more people you can help, the better.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 你能帮助的人越多越好。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: But friends should be your compass.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 但朋友应该是你的指南针。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 5 ] Donald Hall said young would-be poets were mistaken to be so obsessed with being published.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [5]唐纳德·霍尔说，年轻的诗歌写作者如此执着于发表作品，是一种错误。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: But you can imagine what it would do for a 24 year old to get a poem published in The New Yorker .
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 但你可以想象，对一个二十四岁的人来说，在《纽约客》发表一首诗意味着什么。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Now to people he meets at parties he's a real poet.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 现在，聚会上遇见的人会把他当作真正的诗人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Actually he's no better or worse than he was before, but to a clueless audience like that, the approval of an official authority makes all the difference.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 其实，他既没有比以前更好，也没有更差；但对于那些不懂诗的受众，权威机构的认可却能改变一切。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: So it's a harder problem than Hall realizes.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 所以，这个问题比霍尔意识到的更难。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: The reason the young care so much about prestige is that the people they want to impress are not very discerning.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 年轻人如此在意名望，是因为他们想打动的人并没有多强的鉴赏力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 6 ] This is isomorphic to the principle that you should prevent your beliefs about how things are from being contaminated by how you wish they were.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [6]这与另一条原则具有相同的结构：不要让“你希望事情是什么样”污染你对“事情实际上是什么样”的判断。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Most people let them mix pretty promiscuously.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 大多数人会任由这两者随意混在一起。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: The continuing popularity of religion is the most visible index of that.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 宗教持续受到欢迎，就是最明显的指标。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: [ 7 ] A more accurate metaphor would be to say that the graph of jobs is not very well connected.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: [7]更准确的比喻是：各种工作构成的图，其连接并不充分。

gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.en: Thanks to Trevor Blackwell, Dan Friedman, Sarah Harlin, Jessica Livingston, Jackie McDonough, Robert Morris, Peter Norvig, David Sloo, and Aaron Swartz for reading drafts of this.
gr-pg-how-to-do-what-you-love.cn: 感谢特雷弗·布莱克韦尔、丹·弗里德曼、莎拉·哈林、杰西卡·利文斯顿、杰姬·麦克多诺、罗伯特·莫里斯、彼得·诺维格、戴维·斯卢和亚伦·斯沃茨阅读本文草稿。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you collected lists of techniques for doing great work in a lot of different fields, what would the intersection look like?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 试想，若将各个领域成就卓越的方法收集起来，它们的交集会呈现出怎样的面貌？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I decided to find out by making it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 为了寻找答案，我决定尝试梳理一番。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Partly my goal was to create a guide that could be used by someone working in any field.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我的初衷是为各行各业的从业者提供一份通用指南。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But I was also curious about the shape of the intersection.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但我同样好奇，这些方法的交集究竟为何物？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And one thing this exercise shows is that it does have a definite shape; it's not just a point labelled "work hard."
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 梳理之后，我发现其轮廓十分清晰，绝非“努力工作”这四个字所能概括。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The following recipe assumes you're very ambitious.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 下文是写给那些有雄心壮志之人看的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The first step is to decide what to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 第一步是决定“做什么”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The work you choose needs to have three qualities: it has to be something you have a natural aptitude for, that you have a deep interest in, and that offers scope to do great work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你选择的工作需同时满足三个条件：天赋：你本就擅长此事；热情：你对它有着极深厚的兴趣；潜力：它拥有成就卓越的广阔空间。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In practice you don't have to worry much about the third criterion.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 实际上，你大可不必过分纠结第三点。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Ambitious people are if anything already too conservative about it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有雄心的人往往容易低估自己，行事偏于保守。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So all you need to do is find something you have an aptitude for and great interest in. [ 1 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 因此，只需专注于前两点：找到那些既能发挥你天赋，又能让你深深着迷的事。[1]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That sounds straightforward, but it's often quite difficult.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这听起来简单，行之维艰。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you're young you don't know what you're good at or what different kinds of work are like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 年轻时，你往往既不了解自己的长处，也不清楚各种工作的真实面貌。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Some kinds of work you end up doing may not even exist yet.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有些工作甚至尚未诞生。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So while some people know what they want to do at 14, most have to figure it out.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 虽有人早在 14 岁便笃定方向，但大多数人仍需在摸索中寻找答案。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The way to figure out what to work on is by working.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 弄清自己该做什么的方法，就是动手去做。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you're not sure what to work on, guess.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果不确定要做什么，就先猜一个方向。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But pick something and get going.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但要选定一件事，然后开始行动。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You'll probably guess wrong some of the time, but that's fine.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有时你可能会猜错，不过这没关系。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's good to know about multiple things; some of the biggest discoveries come from noticing connections between different fields.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 了解多个领域是好事；有些最重大的发现，正是来自发现不同领域之间的联系。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Develop a habit of working on your own projects.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 养成做自己项目的习惯。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't let "work" mean something other people tell you to do.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 别让“工作”仅仅意味着别人叫你做的事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you do manage to do great work one day, it will probably be on a project of your own.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果有一天你真的做出了伟大的成果，很可能是在你自己的项目中。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It may be within some bigger project, but you'll be driving your part of it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这个项目也许属于某个更大的项目，但你会主导自己负责的那一部分。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What should your projects be?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你该做什么项目？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Whatever seems to you excitingly ambitious.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 任何让你因其雄心而感到兴奋的项目。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: As you grow older and your taste in projects evolves, exciting and important will converge.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 随着年龄增长、对项目的品味不断变化，“令人兴奋”和“重要”会逐渐重合。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: At 7 it may seem excitingly ambitious to build huge things out of Lego, then at 14 to teach yourself calculus, till at 21 you're starting to explore unanswered questions in physics.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 七岁时，用乐高搭建巨大的东西可能令人兴奋；十四岁时是自学微积分；到了二十一岁，则可能开始探索物理学中尚未解答的问题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But always preserve excitingness.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但无论何时，都要保留那份兴奋感。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There's a kind of excited curiosity that's both the engine and the rudder of great work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有一种令人兴奋的好奇心，既是伟大工作的引擎，也是它的舵。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It will not only drive you, but if you let it have its way, will also show you what to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它不仅会推动你；如果你让它自由发展，它还会指引你该做什么。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What are you excessively curious about — curious to a degree that would bore most other people?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有什么事是旁人倍感无聊，你却兴致盎然的？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's what you're looking for.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这就是你要找的答案。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Once you've found something you're excessively interested in, the next step is to learn enough about it to get you to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一旦锁定了那个让你极度着迷的领域，下一步就是通过学习，抵达人类知识的疆界。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Knowledge expands fractally, and from a distance its edges look smooth, but once you learn enough to get close to one, they turn out to be full of gaps.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 知识具有分形（Fractal）结构：远观轮廓平滑，一旦你掌握了足够多的知识并逼近边界，就会发现那里其实布满了缺口。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The next step is to notice them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 接下来的任务便是去“看见”这些缺口。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This takes some skill, because your brain wants to ignore such gaps in order to make a simpler model of the world.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这需要技巧，因为大脑为了构建简化的世界模型，倾向于忽略它们。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Many discoveries have come from asking questions about things that everyone else took for granted. [ 2 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 许多伟大的发现，正是源于对既定认知的质疑。[2]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If the answers seem strange, so much the better.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果答案看起来很怪异，那再好不过。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work often has a tincture of strangeness.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 伟大的工作往往都带有一丝奇异色彩。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You see this from painting to math.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 无论是绘画还是数学，都是如此。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It would be affected to try to manufacture it, but if it appears, embrace it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不必刻意猎奇，但若它自然出现，请欣然拥抱。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Boldly chase outlier ideas, even if other people aren't interested in them — in fact, especially if they aren't.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 大胆追逐那些“离群”的想法，即使——或者说尤其是——其他人都不感兴趣时。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you're excited about some possibility that everyone else ignores, and you have enough expertise to say precisely what they're all overlooking, that's as good a bet as you'll find. [ 3 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你对某种可能性感到兴奋，而旁人视而不见，且你有足够的专业知识指出他们的疏漏，那么这很可能就是你一直在寻找的最佳良机。[3]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Four steps: choose a field, learn enough to get to the frontier, notice gaps, explore promising ones.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 选定领域；学至前沿；发现缺口；探索有希望的缺口。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This is how practically everyone who's done great work has done it, from painters to physicists.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 从画家到物理学家，几乎所有成就卓越者都遵循此道。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Steps two and four will require hard work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 第二步和第四步需要艰苦卓绝的努力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It may not be possible to prove that you have to work hard to do great things, but the empirical evidence is on the scale of the evidence for mortality.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 虽然未必能从逻辑上证明“卓越必须苦干”，但经验法则就如同生老病死般确凿。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's why it's essential to work on something you're deeply interested in.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 正因如此，你必须从事自己深感兴趣的工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Interest will drive you to work harder than mere diligence ever could.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 比起纯粹的勤奋，兴趣才是驱动你全力以赴的更强动力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The three most powerful motives are curiosity, delight, and the desire to do something impressive.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 好奇心、愉悦感，以及成就伟业的渴望，是三股最强大的驱动力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Sometimes they converge, and that combination is the most powerful of all.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当这三者交汇，爆发出的能量将无穷无尽。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The big prize is to discover a new fractal bud.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 终极奖赏在于发现一个新的“分形芽”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You notice a crack in the surface of knowledge, pry it open, and there's a whole world inside.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你在知识的表面窥见一道裂缝，撬开它，里面竟藏着一个全新的世界。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Let's talk a little more about the complicated business of figuring out what to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 让我们深入审视“决定做什么”这道难题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The main reason it's hard is that you can't tell what most kinds of work are like except by doing them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 其棘手之处在于，除了亲身试错，你很难真正洞悉一份工作的全貌。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Which means the four steps overlap: you may have to work at something for years before you know how much you like it or how good you are at it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这意味着前述的四个步骤往往是交织重叠的：你可能需要投入数年，方能知晓自己是否真心喜爱、或擅长某事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And in the meantime you're not doing, and thus not learning about, most other kinds of work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 与此同时，你没有在从事大多数其他类型的工作，因此也无从了解它们。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So in the worst case you choose late based on very incomplete information. [ 4 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，最坏的情况是：你很晚才做出选择，而且依据的信息还很不完整。[4]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The nature of ambition exacerbates this problem.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 野心的本质加剧了这一困境。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Ambition comes in two forms, one that precedes interest in the subject and one that grows out of it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 野心分两种：一种先于兴趣存在，一种由兴趣滋生。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Most people who do great work have a mix, and the more you have of the former, the harder it will be to decide what to do.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 大多数成就卓越者兼而有之，但前一种野心越重，决策便越难。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The educational systems in most countries pretend it's easy.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 各国教育系统大多对这一难题粉饰太平。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They expect you to commit to a field long before you could know what it's really like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它们强迫你在窥见学科全貌之前便选定方向。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And as a result an ambitious person on an optimal trajectory will often read to the system as an instance of breakage.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 结果导致，一个本在最优路径上行进的有志青年，往往被系统判定为“异类”或“残次品”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It would be better if they at least admitted it — if they admitted that the system not only can't do much to help you figure out what to work on, but is designed on the assumption that you'll somehow magically guess as a teenager.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 若教育系统能坦诚相告就好了——承认它不仅爱莫能助，其设计初衷更是建立在“青少年能奇迹般猜对方向”这一假设之上。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They don't tell you, but I will: when it comes to figuring out what to work on, you're on your own.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它们不会告诉你，但我会：在决定“做什么”这件事上，你只能孤军奋战。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Some people get lucky and do guess correctly, but the rest will find themselves scrambling diagonally across tracks laid down on the assumption that everyone does.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有些人运气好猜对了，而剩下的人，只能在一条预设所有人都已选对的轨道上，逆势横穿，踉跄前行。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What should you do if you're young and ambitious but don't know what to work on?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你年轻、雄心勃勃却又迷茫无措，该怎么办？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What you should not do is drift along passively, assuming the problem will solve itself.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 最忌讳的便是随波逐流，妄想问题会自行消解。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You need to take action.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你必须行动。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But there is no systematic procedure you can follow.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但这并无标准定式。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you read biographies of people who've done great work, it's remarkable how much luck is involved.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 读读伟人传记，你会惊讶地发现“运气”占据了多大比重。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They discover what to work on as a result of a chance meeting, or by reading a book they happen to pick up.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一次偶遇、一本闲书，都可能成为指路明灯。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So you need to make yourself a big target for luck, and the way to do that is to be curious.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 因此，你需要让自己成为好运容易命中的“靶子”，而方法就是保持好奇。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Try lots of things, meet lots of people, read lots of books, ask lots of questions. [ 5 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 多尝试，多见人，多读书，多提问。[5]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When in doubt, optimize for interestingness.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 犹豫时，优先选择更有趣的方向。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Fields change as you learn more about them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 随着了解加深，一个领域在你眼中的样子会发生变化。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What mathematicians do, for example, is very different from what you do in high school math classes.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 比如，数学家做的事，与高中数学课上做的事截然不同。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So you need to give different types of work a chance to show you what they're like.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 因此，你需要给不同类型的工作机会，让它们展现真实的样子。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But a field should become increasingly interesting as you learn more about it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，随着了解加深，一个领域应该变得越来越有趣。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If it doesn't, it's probably not for you.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果没有，它可能就不适合你。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't worry if you find you're interested in different things than other people.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 若你的兴趣点异于常人，别担心。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The stranger your tastes in interestingness, the better.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 品味越怪，越是好事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Strange tastes are often strong ones, and a strong taste for work means you'll be productive.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 怪诞的品味通常意味着强烈的热爱，而热爱是高效产出的前提。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And you're more likely to find new things if you're looking where few have looked before.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 况且，在人迹罕至之地，你更有可能发现新大陆。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One sign that you're suited for some kind of work is when you like even the parts that other people find tedious or frightening.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 判断你是否适合某项工作的一个试金石是：哪怕是旁人觉得枯燥甚至畏惧的部分，你也乐在其中。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But fields aren't people; you don't owe them any loyalty.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但领域不是人，你无需对它们“忠诚”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If in the course of working on one thing you discover another that's more exciting, don't be afraid to switch.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 若在研究某事的过程中发现了更令人兴奋的新方向，别害怕，尽管去追。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you're making something for people, make sure it's something they actually want.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你的工作是创造事物，请确保那是人们真正想要的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The best way to do this is to make something you yourself want.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 最佳捷径便是做你自己想用的东西。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Write the story you want to read; build the tool you want to use.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 写你想读的故事，造你想用的工具。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Since your friends probably have similar interests, this will also get you your initial audience.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 既然你的朋友往往与你志趣相投，这也能助你获得最初的用户群。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This should follow from the excitingness rule.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这其实契合了“兴奋感法则”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Obviously the most exciting story to write will be the one you want to read.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 显而易见，写起来最让你兴奋的故事，正是你自己最想读的那一个。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The reason I mention this case explicitly is that so many people get it wrong.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我之所以特意强调此点，是因为太多人本末倒置。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Instead of making what they want, they try to make what some imaginary, more sophisticated audience wants.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他们不去做自己想要的，而是试图迎合某个想象中更为“高深”的受众群体。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And once you go down that route, you're lost. [ 6 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一旦走上那条路，你就迷失了。[6]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There are a lot of forces that will lead you astray when you're trying to figure out what to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在弄清自己该做什么的过程中，有许多力量会把你引向歧途。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Pretentiousness, fashion, fear, money, politics, other people's wishes, eminent frauds.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 比如矫揉造作、时尚、恐惧、金钱、政治、他人的期望，以及声名显赫的骗子。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But if you stick to what you find genuinely interesting, you'll be proof against all of them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但只要坚守你真正感兴趣的事物，这一切都无法撼动你。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you're interested, you're not astray.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 只要兴趣尚存，你就未曾迷路。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Following your interests may sound like a rather passive strategy, but in practice it usually means following them past all sorts of obstacles.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 循兴趣而行，初听似乎是被动的策略，但在实践中，这往往意味着你要追随兴趣，跨越重重阻碍。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You usually have to risk rejection and failure.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你常需直面被拒与失败的风险。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So it does take a good deal of boldness.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 因此，这实则需要极大的 胆识。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But while you need boldness, you don't usually need much planning.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 胆识虽不可或缺，周详的规划却往往多余。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In most cases the recipe for doing great work is simply: work hard on excitingly ambitious projects, and something good will come of it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 多数情况下，成就卓越的秘诀非常简单：在那些既令人兴奋又充满野心的项目上努力工作，好事自会发生。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Instead of making a plan and then executing it, you just try to preserve certain invariants.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 与其制定缜密的计划并刻板执行，不如坚守几条核心的“不变量”（invariants）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The trouble with planning is that it only works for achievements you can describe in advance.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 规划的弊病在于，它仅适用于那些可被预先定义的成就。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You can win a gold medal or get rich by deciding to as a child and then tenaciously pursuing that goal, but you can't discover natural selection that way.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 若你立志夺得金牌或发家致富，凭坚韧执行确有望达成；但你无法以此发现“自然选择”定律。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I think for most people who want to do great work, the right strategy is not to plan too much.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我认为对于大多数渴望成就卓越的人来说，最佳策略是 切勿过度规划。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: At each stage do whatever seems most interesting and gives you the best options for the future.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在每一阶段，只做当时觉得最有趣、且最能为未来增加选项的事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I call this approach "staying upwind." This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我把这种方法称为‘保持上风’。大多数做出伟大成果的人，似乎都是这么做的。

alignedParts.en: I call this approach "staying upwind."
alignedParts.cn: 我把这种方法称为‘保持上风’。

alignedParts.en: This is how most people who've done great work seem to have done it.
alignedParts.cn: 大多数做出伟大成果的人，似乎都是这么做的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Even when you've found something exciting to work on, working on it is not always straightforward.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 即使找到了令人兴奋的方向，实际执行起来也未必总是一帆风顺。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There will be times when some new idea makes you leap out of bed in the morning and get straight to work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有时，一个新想法会让你清晨从床上一跃而起，立刻开始工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But there will also be plenty of times when things aren't like that.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但也不乏万事滞涩的时刻。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You don't just put out your sail and get blown forward by inspiration.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你不能指望升起帆，便坐等灵感之风送你抵达终点。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There are headwinds and currents and hidden shoals.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 海上有逆风、暗流，亦有暗礁。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So there's a technique to working, just as there is to sailing.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 工作如航海，是讲究技术的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: For example, while you must work hard, it's possible to work too hard, and if you do that you'll find you get diminishing returns: fatigue will make you stupid, and eventually even damage your health.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 例如，虽需努力，但也存在“过犹不及”一说。一旦越界，便会出现边际效益递减：疲劳会让你变得迟钝，甚至损害健康。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The point at which work yields diminishing returns depends on the type.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 边际效益递减的临界点取决于工作类型。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Some of the hardest types you might only be able to do for four or five hours a day.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 对于那些最耗神的工作，你一天的高效时间或许只有四五个小时。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Ideally those hours will be contiguous.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 理想情况下，这些时间应是连续的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: To the extent you can, try to arrange your life so you have big blocks of time to work in.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 尽量安排好生活，让自己拥有大块连续的工作时间。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You'll shy away from hard tasks if you know you might be interrupted.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果知道随时可能被打断，你就会回避困难的任务。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It will probably be harder to start working than to keep working.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: “启动”往往比“持续”更难。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You'll often have to trick yourself to get over that initial threshold.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你经常需要哄骗自己一下，以跨过最初的门槛。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't worry about this; it's the nature of work, not a flaw in your character.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 别担心，这是工作的固有属性，并非你性格有缺。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Work has a sort of activation energy, both per day and per project.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 工作存在一种“活化能”（activation energy），无论是按天还是按项目计算皆是如此。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And since this threshold is fake in the sense that it's higher than the energy required to keep going, it's ok to tell yourself a lie of corresponding magnitude to get over it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这个门槛在某种意义上是虚高的，因为启动所需的能量大于持续工作所需的能量；因此，为了跨过它，对自己撒个相应程度的谎也无妨。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's usually a mistake to lie to yourself if you want to do great work, but this is one of the rare cases where it isn't.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 想做出伟大的成果，通常不该自欺欺人，但这正是少数例外之一。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far." Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 早晨不想开始工作时，我常常骗自己说：‘我就把已经写好的内容读一遍。’五分钟后，我就发现了错误或不完整的地方，接着便开始干了。

alignedParts.en: When I'm reluctant to start work in the morning, I often trick myself by saying "I'll just read over what I've got so far."
alignedParts.cn: 早晨不想开始工作时，我常常骗自己说：‘我就把已经写好的内容读一遍。’

alignedParts.en: Five minutes later I've found something that seems mistaken or incomplete, and I'm off.
alignedParts.cn: 五分钟后，我就发现了错误或不完整的地方，接着便开始干了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Similar techniques work for starting new projects.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 类似的技巧也适用于启动新项目。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's ok to lie to yourself about how much work a project will entail, for example.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 比如，对所需的工作量撒点谎也无伤大雅。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Lots of great things began with someone saying "How hard could it be?"
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 许多伟大的成就都始于这句名言：“这能有多难？”

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This is one case where the young have an advantage.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这是年轻人拥有优势的一个特例。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They're more optimistic, and even though one of the sources of their optimism is ignorance, in this case ignorance can sometimes beat knowledge.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他们更乐观，虽说这种乐观部分源于无知，但在此刻，无知有时竟能胜过博学。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Try to finish what you start, though, even if it turns out to be more work than you expected.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，一旦开始，就要尽力完成，哪怕工作量超出了预期。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Finishing things is not just an exercise in tidiness or self-discipline.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 善始善终不仅关乎整洁与自律。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In many projects a lot of the best work happens in what was meant to be the final stage.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在许多项目中，最精彩的发现往往诞生于原以为是收尾的阶段。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Another permissible lie is to exaggerate the importance of what you're working on, at least in your own mind.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 另一个被允许的谎言是，夸大你手头工作的重要性——至少在你自己心里。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If that helps you discover something new, it may turn out not to have been a lie after all. [ 7 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果这能助你发现新事物，那它最终可能就不再是一个谎言了。[7]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Since there are two senses of starting work — per day and per project — there are also two forms of procrastination.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 既然工作的启动可分为“按日”和“按项目”两类，拖延症便也有两种形式。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Per-project procrastination is far the more dangerous.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 其中，“项目型拖延”尤为凶险。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You put off starting that ambitious project from year to year because the time isn't quite right.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你年复一年地推迟那个宏大的计划，总以此际“时机未到”自我开脱。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you're procrastinating in units of years, you can get a lot not done. [ 8 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一旦拖延的单位变成了“年”，你错失的将不可估量。[8]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One reason per-project procrastination is so dangerous is that it usually camouflages itself as work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: “项目型拖延”之所以致命，因其常披着“工作”的外衣。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You're not just sitting around doing nothing; you're working industriously on something else.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你并非游手好闲，甚至可能正兢兢业业地处理着其他琐事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So per-project procrastination doesn't set off the alarms that per-day procrastination does.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，按项目拖延不会像按天拖延那样触发警报。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You're too busy to notice it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你忙得根本注意不到它。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The way to beat it is to stop occasionally and ask yourself: Am I working on what I most want to work on?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 破解之法是时不时停下来自问：我正在做那件我最想做的事吗？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you're young it's ok if the answer is sometimes no, but this gets increasingly dangerous as you get older. [ 9 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 年轻时，答“否”尚可原谅；但随着年岁渐长，这个答案将愈发危险。[9]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work usually entails spending what would seem to most people an unreasonable amount of time on a problem.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 伟大的工作，往往意味着在一个问题上投入常人眼中“不合理”的时间。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You can't think of this time as a cost, or it will seem too high.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你不能将其视作代价，否则这笔账未免太不划算。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You have to find the work sufficiently engaging as it's happening.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你必须在过程中就感受到其迷人之处。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There may be some jobs where you have to work diligently for years at things you hate before you get to the good part, but this is not how great work happens.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 诚然，有些工作需先忍受多年的枯燥方能苦尽甘来，但这并非成就卓越的通途。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work happens by focusing consistently on something you're genuinely interested in.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 卓越源于持续专注于你真正感兴趣的事物。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you pause to take stock, you're surprised how far you've come.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你驻足回望，往往会惊讶于自己竟已行进至此。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The reason we're surprised is that we underestimate the cumulative effect of work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我们之所以惊讶，是因为低估了工作的累积之功。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Writing a page a day doesn't sound like much, but if you do it every day you'll write a book a year.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 每天写一页听起来不多，但如果天天坚持，一年就能写出一本书。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's the key: consistency.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 关键就在这里：持续不断。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: People who do great things don't get a lot done every day.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 成就非凡的人，并不是每天都完成很多事情。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They get something done, rather than nothing.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他们每天都会完成一些事，而不是一事无成。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you do work that compounds, you'll get exponential growth.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你的工作能不断产生复利效应，就会获得指数式增长。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Most people who do this do it unconsciously, but it's worth stopping to think about.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 大多数这样做的人并非有意为之，但这值得停下来想一想。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Learning, for example, is an instance of this phenomenon: the more you learn about something, the easier it is to learn more.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 比如，学习就是这种现象：对某件事了解得越多，继续深入学习就越容易。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Growing an audience is another: the more fans you have, the more new fans they'll bring you.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 积累受众亦是如此：粉丝越多，带来的新粉丝便越多。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The trouble with exponential growth is that the curve feels flat in the beginning.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 指数式增长的问题在于，曲线起初看起来很平。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It isn't; it's still a wonderful exponential curve.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 其实不是，它仍然是一条美妙的指数曲线。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But we can't grasp that intuitively, so we underrate exponential growth in its early stages.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但我们的直觉无法捕捉微小的起势，因此往往低估了初期的增长。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Something that grows exponentially can become so valuable that it's worth making an extraordinary effort to get it started.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 具有指数潜力的事物价值连城，值得付出非凡努力去启动。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But since we underrate exponential growth early on, this too is mostly done unconsciously: people push through the initial, unrewarding phase of learning something new because they know from experience that learning new things always takes an initial push, or they grow their audience one fan at a time because they have nothing better to do.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但正因初期常被看轻，这通常也是在无意识中完成的：人们熬过学习新知初期那段毫无回报的阶段，是因经验告知这只是暂时；或者他们一个接一个地积累粉丝，仅仅是因为当时无事可做。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If people consciously realized they could invest in exponential growth, many more would do it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 若人们能有意识地认知到投资“指数级增长”的价值，定会有更多人投身其中。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Work doesn't just happen when you're trying to.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 工作并不止于伏案苦干之时。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There's a kind of undirected thinking you do when walking or taking a shower or lying in bed that can be very powerful.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你散步、沐浴或安寝时，发散的思维往往力大无穷。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: By letting your mind wander a little, you'll often solve problems you were unable to solve by frontal attack.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 稍微让思绪游走，往往能解决那些正面攻克不了的问题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You have to be working hard in the normal way to benefit from this phenomenon, though.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，要从这种现象中受益，你也必须以通常的方式努力工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You can't just walk around daydreaming.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你不能只是一边闲逛一边做白日梦。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The daydreaming has to be interleaved with deliberate work that feeds it questions. [ 10 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 白日梦必须与有意识的工作交替进行，由后者为它提供问题。[10]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Everyone knows to avoid distractions at work, but it's also important to avoid them in the other half of the cycle.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 众皆知工作时需心无旁骛，殊不知在循环的另一半（休息/发散）中避免分心同样关键。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you let your mind wander, it wanders to whatever you care about most at that moment.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当思绪游离，它会飘向你此刻最挂怀之事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So avoid the kind of distraction that pushes your work out of the top spot, or you'll waste this valuable type of thinking on the distraction instead.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，要避免那些把工作挤出关注首位的干扰，否则这种宝贵的思考方式，就会被浪费在干扰上。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: (Exception: Don't avoid love.)
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: （例外：不要回避爱情。）

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Consciously cultivate your taste in the work done in your field.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要有意识地培养对本领域工作的品味。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Until you know which is the best and what makes it so, you don't know what you're aiming for.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 直至知晓何为最佳、因何最佳，方知瞄准何处。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And that is what you're aiming for, because if you don't try to be the best, you won't even be good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这必须是你的目标，因为若不试着成为最佳，你甚至连“好”都做不到。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This observation has been made by so many people in so many different fields that it might be worth thinking about why it's true.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不同领域的许多人都做过这种观察，因此值得想想它为什么成立。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It could be because ambition is a phenomenon where almost all the error is in one direction — where almost all the shells that miss the target miss by falling short.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 也许是因为，关于抱负的误差几乎都朝同一个方向：几乎所有没打中目标的炮弹，都是因为射得不够远。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Or it could be because ambition to be the best is a qualitatively different thing from ambition to be good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 或许是因为“想成为最好”与“想做得不错”有着质的区别。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Or maybe being good is simply too vague a standard.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 又或许仅仅是因为“做得不错”这一标准太过模糊。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Probably all three are true. [ 11 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 大概三者皆有之。[11]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Fortunately there's a kind of economy of scale here.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所幸，此处存在一种规模经济。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Though it might seem like you'd be taking on a heavy burden by trying to be the best, in practice you often end up net ahead.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 虽然争取做到最好看起来像给自己加上重担，但实际上，最终往往是收益大于负担。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's exciting, and also strangely liberating.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它既令人兴奋，又有一种奇妙的解放感。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It simplifies things.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它让事情变得简单。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In some ways it's easier to try to be the best than to try merely to be good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在某些方面，努力成为最好，反而比只求做得不错更容易。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One way to aim high is to try to make something that people will care about in a hundred years.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个拔高目标的方法是：试着做出百年之后人们依然在乎的东西。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Not because their opinions matter more than your contemporaries', but because something that still seems good in a hundred years is more likely to be genuinely good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这并非因为后人的看法比同时代人更重要，而是因为经得起百年考验的东西，更可能是真正的好东西。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't try to work in a distinctive style.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不要刻意追求独特的风格。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Just try to do the best job you can; you won't be able to help doing it in a distinctive way.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你只需全力以赴做到最好，独特的风格自然会随之而来，你想拦都拦不住。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Style is doing things in a distinctive way without trying to.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所谓的“风格”，就是你在不经意间做事的独特方式。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Trying to is affectation.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 刻意为之，那是 矫揉造作 （Affectation）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Affectation is in effect to pretend that someone other than you is doing the work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 矫揉造作，本质上是在假装“不是你”的人在做这份工作。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You adopt an impressive but fake persona, and while you're pleased with the impressiveness, the fakeness is what shows in the work. [ 12 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你戴上了一副令人印象深刻但虚假的面具。虽然你对那副面具很满意，但最终显露在作品里的，只有那份“虚假”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The temptation to be someone else is greatest for the young.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: [12]年轻人最容易陷入这种诱惑，想变成别人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They often feel like nobodies.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 因为他们觉得自己是个无名小卒。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But you never need to worry about that problem, because it's self-solving if you work on sufficiently ambitious projects.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但你完全不必为此焦虑，只要你致力于足够有野心的项目，这个问题便会迎刃而解。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you succeed at an ambitious project, you're not a nobody; you're the person who did it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你做成了一个雄心勃勃的项目，你就不再是无名小卒；你就是那个把它做成的人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So just do the work and your identity will take care of itself.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，只管去做，你的身份自会随之确立。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: "Avoid affectation" is a useful rule so far as it goes, but how would you express this idea positively?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: “避免矫揉造作”是个有用的负面规则，但如果我们要用正面的语言来表达呢？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: How would you say what to be, instead of what not to be?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果不说“不要做什么”，而说“要做什么”呢？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The best answer is earnest.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 最好的答案是：真诚 （Earnest）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you're earnest you avoid not just affectation but a whole set of similar vices.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你足够真诚，你不仅能避免矫揉造作，还能避开一大堆类似的毛病。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The core of being earnest is being intellectually honest.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 真诚的核心是 智识上的诚实 （Intellectual Honesty）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: We're taught as children to be honest as an unselfish virtue — as a kind of sacrifice.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 小时候，我们被教育诚实是一种无私的美德，是一种牺牲。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But in fact it's a source of power too.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但事实上，诚实也是一种力量的源泉。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: To see new ideas, you need an exceptionally sharp eye for the truth.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要发现新观点，你需要一双极其锐利、能洞察真相的眼睛。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You're trying to see more truth than others have seen so far.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你正试图看到别人未曾看到的真相。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And how can you have a sharp eye for the truth if you're intellectually dishonest?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你在智识上不诚实，又怎能拥有这双锐眼？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One way to avoid intellectual dishonesty is to maintain a slight positive pressure in the opposite direction.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 避免智识不诚实的一个方法是，在反方向上保持一点“正压”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Be aggressively willing to admit that you're mistaken.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要极其主动地承认自己的错误。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Once you've admitted you were mistaken about something, you're free.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一旦承认自己在某件事上错了，你就自由了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Till then you have to carry it. [ 13 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在此之前，你都得背着那个错误。[13]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Another more subtle component of earnestness is informality.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 真诚还有一个更微妙的组成部分：不拘形式。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Informality is much more important than its grammatically negative name implies.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它的重要性远超其字面上的“否定”意味所暗示的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's not merely the absence of something.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它并不只是缺少某种东西。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It means focusing on what matters instead of what doesn't.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 而是指：专注于重要之事，忽略无关紧要之事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What formality and affectation have in common is that as well as doing the work, you're trying to seem a certain way as you're doing it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 形式主义和矫揉造作的共同点在于：你在做事的同时，还试图在做的过程中表现出某种特定的样子。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But any energy that goes into how you seem comes out of being good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但任何用于“装样子”的能量，都是从“把事做好”的能量中抽走的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's one reason nerds have an advantage in doing great work: they expend little effort on seeming anything.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这就是为什么极客（Nerds）在成就卓越方面拥有优势：他们很少花心思去装样子。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In fact that's basically the definition of a nerd.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 事实上，这基本就是“极客”的定义。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Nerds have a kind of innocent boldness that's exactly what you need in doing great work.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 极客有一种天真而大胆的气质，这正是做出伟大成果所需要的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's not learned; it's preserved from childhood.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它不是后来学会的，而是从童年保留下来的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So hold onto it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，请守住它。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Be the one who puts things out there rather than the one who sits back and offers sophisticated-sounding criticisms of them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 做一个把东西做出来并公之于众的人，而不是坐在后面发表高深批评的人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: "It's easy to criticize" is true in the most literal sense, and the route to great work is never easy.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: “批评很容易”这句话在字面意义上也是对的，通往卓越的道路从来都不容易。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There may be some jobs where it's an advantage to be cynical and pessimistic, but if you want to do great work it's an advantage to be optimistic, even though that means you'll risk looking like a fool sometimes.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 也许在某些工作中，愤世嫉俗和悲观主义是优势，但如果你想成就卓越，乐观才是优势，哪怕这意味着你有时候看起来像个傻瓜。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There's an old tradition of doing the opposite.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 古老的传统总是教导我们要反其道而行之。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The Old Testament says it's better to keep quiet lest you look like a fool.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 《旧约》说要保持沉默，以免看起来像个傻瓜。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But that's advice for seeming smart.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但那是教你如何 显得 聪明。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you actually want to discover new things, it's better to take the risk of telling people your ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你真的想发现新事物，最好还是冒点险，把你的想法告诉别人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Some people are naturally earnest, and with others it takes a conscious effort.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有些人天生真诚，有些人则需要刻意练习。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Either kind of earnestness will suffice.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 两种真诚都可以。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But I doubt it would be possible to do great work without being earnest.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但我怀疑，不真诚的人能否做出伟大的成果。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's so hard to do even if you are.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 即使足够真诚，要做到这一点也已经很难了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You don't have enough margin for error to accommodate the distortions introduced by being affected, intellectually dishonest, orthodox, fashionable, or cool. [ 14 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你没有足够的容错空间，去承受矫揉造作、思想上的不诚实、墨守成规、追逐时尚或装酷所带来的扭曲。[14]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work is consistent not only with who did it, but with itself.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 卓越的作品不仅与其作者保持一致，其内部也必须协调统一。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's usually all of a piece.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它通常是一个整体。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So if you face a decision in the middle of working on something, ask which choice is more consistent.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，如果在工作中面临抉择，问问自己：哪个选择能让整体更协调？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You may have to throw things away and redo them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你可能需要把做好的东西扔掉重来。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You won't necessarily have to, but you have to be willing to.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不一定非得这么做，但你必须 愿意 这么做。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And that can take some effort; when there's something you need to redo, status quo bias and laziness will combine to keep you in denial about it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这可能需要一些努力；当某件事需要重做时，维持现状的偏见和懒惰会联手，让你不愿承认这一点。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: To beat this ask: If I'd already made the change, would I want to revert to what I have now?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要克服它们，可以问自己：如果我已经做了这个改变，还会想改回现在的样子吗？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Have the confidence to cut.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要有 做减法 （Cut）的自信。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't keep something that doesn't fit just because you're proud of it, or because it cost you a lot of effort.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不要仅仅因为你为之感到自豪，或付出了巨大努力，就保留那些不合适的部分。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Indeed, in some kinds of work it's good to strip whatever you're doing to its essence.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 实际上，在某些工作中，将要做的事情剥离到只剩本质是件好事。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The result will be more concentrated; you'll understand it better; and you won't be able to lie to yourself about whether there's anything real there.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 结果会更浓缩，你会理解得更透彻，而且你无法再欺骗自己这里面是否有真材实料。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Mathematical elegance may sound like a mere metaphor, drawn from the arts.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 数学上的优雅 （Mathematical Elegance）听起来像是一个源自艺术的隐喻。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's what I thought when I first heard the term "elegant" applied to a proof.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当我第一次听到用“优雅”来形容数学证明时，我也是这么想的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But now I suspect it's conceptually prior — that the main ingredient in artistic elegance is mathematical elegance.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但我现在怀疑，它在概念上其实是先于艺术的——艺术优雅的主要成分其实就是数学优雅。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: At any rate it's a useful standard well beyond math.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 无论如何，这是一个超越数学领域的有用标准。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Elegance can be a long-term bet, though.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，追求优雅可能是一项长期赌注。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Laborious solutions will often have more prestige in the short term.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 从短期看，费力的解决方案往往更具声望。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They cost a lot of effort and they're hard to understand, both of which impress people, at least temporarily.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它们耗费巨大心力，且难以理解，这两点都能唬住人——至少暂时能。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Whereas some of the very best work will seem like it took comparatively little effort, because it was in a sense already there.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 相反，一些最顶尖的工作看起来似乎没费什么劲，因为它在某种意义上 本来就在那里。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It didn't have to be built, just seen.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它不需要被建造，只需要被看见。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's a very good sign when it's hard to say whether you're creating something or discovering it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你很难分清你是在创造还是在发现时，这是一个非常好的信号。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you're doing work that could be seen as either creation or discovery, err on the side of discovery.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你做的工作既可被视为创造也可被视为发现时，倾向于将其视为发现。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Try thinking of yourself as a mere conduit through which the ideas take their natural shape.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 试着把自己想象成一个管道，思想通过你呈现出它们自然的形状。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: (Strangely enough, one exception is the problem of choosing a problem to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: （奇怪的是，唯一的例外是“选择做什么”这个问题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This is usually seen as search, but in the best case it's more like creating something.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这通常被视为一种搜索，但在最好的情况下，它更像是一种创造。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In the best case you create the field in the process of exploring it.)
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在最好的情况下，你在探索的过程中创造了这个领域。）

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Similarly, if you're trying to build a powerful tool, make it gratuitously unrestrictive.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 同样，如果你试图构建一个强大的工具，要让它毫无理由地不设限。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: A powerful tool almost by definition will be used in ways you didn't expect, so err on the side of eliminating restrictions, even if you don't know what the benefit will be.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个强大的工具，几乎根据定义，都会被用于你意想不到的方式。所以，哪怕你不知道好处是什么，也要倾向于消除限制。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work will often be tool-like in the sense of being something others build on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 伟大的工作往往具有工具属性，即它是其他人构建事物的基石。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So it's a good sign if you're creating ideas that others could use, or exposing questions that others could answer.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以，如果你正在创造别人可以使用的想法，或者提出别人可以回答的问题，这是个好兆头。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The best ideas have implications in many different areas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 最好的想法在许多不同领域都有其含义。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you express your ideas in the most general form, they'll be truer than you intended.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果用最一般的形式表达想法，它们的正确性会超出你原本设想的范围。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: True by itself is not enough, of course.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当然，仅仅正确还不够。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great ideas have to be true and new.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 伟大的想法必须既正确，又新颖。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And it takes a certain amount of ability to see new ideas even once you've learned enough to get to one of the frontiers of knowledge.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 即使你已经学到某个知识领域的前沿，要发现新想法，仍然需要一定的能力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In English we give this ability names like originality, creativity, and imagination.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在英语中，我们将这种能力称为 原创性 （Originality）、创造力 （Creativity）和 想象力 （Imagination）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And it seems reasonable to give it a separate name, because it does seem to some extent a separate skill.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 给它一个单独的名字是合理的，因为它确实在一定程度上是一项独立的技能。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's possible to have a great deal of ability in other respects — to have a great deal of what's often called technical ability — and yet not have much of this.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个人可能在其他方面能力超群——拥有极高的 技术 能力——但这方面却很匮乏。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I've never liked the term "creative process." It seems misleading.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我一直不喜欢‘创作过程’这个说法。它似乎有误导性。

alignedParts.en: I've never liked the term "creative process."
alignedParts.cn: 我一直不喜欢‘创作过程’这个说法。

alignedParts.en: It seems misleading.
alignedParts.cn: 它似乎有误导性。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Originality isn't a process, but a habit of mind.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 原创性不是一个过程，而是一种思维习惯。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Original thinkers throw off new ideas about whatever they focus on, like an angle grinder throwing off sparks.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 原创的思想者无论关注什么，都会迸发出新想法，就像角磨机飞溅出火花一样。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They can't help it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他们忍不住要这么做。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If the thing they're focused on is something they don't understand very well, these new ideas might not be good.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果他们关注的是自己不太了解的事物，这些新想法可能并不怎么样。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One of the most original thinkers I know decided to focus on dating after he got divorced.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我认识的一位最具原创性的思想者，在离婚后决定研究约会。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: He knew roughly as much about dating as the average 15 year old, and the results were spectacularly colorful.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他对约会的了解大概和普通 15 岁少年差不多，结果虽然丰富多彩，却也令人啼笑皆非。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But to see originality separated from expertise like that made its nature all the more clear.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但这让我们更清楚地看到：原创性是可以与专业知识分离的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I don't know if it's possible to cultivate originality, but there are definitely ways to make the most of however much you have.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我不知道原创性是否可以培养，但肯定有办法让你现有的原创性发挥最大价值。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: For example, you're much more likely to have original ideas when you're working on something.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 例如，当你在做具体工作时，比空想更容易产生原创想法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Original ideas don't come from trying to have original ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 原创想法，并不是靠努力想着“我要有原创想法”而来的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They come from trying to build or understand something slightly too difficult. [ 15 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 而是通过“试图建立或理解某个稍微有点难度的东西”得来的。[15]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Talking or writing about the things you're interested in is a good way to generate new ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 谈论或写作 你感兴趣的事情，是产生新想法的好方法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you try to put ideas into words, a missing idea creates a sort of vacuum that draws it out of you.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你试图将思想转化为语言时，缺失的想法会形成某种真空，把它从你的脑海中吸出来。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Indeed, there's a kind of thinking that can only be done by writing.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 事实上，有一种思考只能通过写作来完成。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Changing your context can help.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 改变环境 也有帮助。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: If you visit a new place, you'll often find you have new ideas there.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 到一个新地方，你常会发现新想法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The journey itself often dislodges them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 旅途本身往往能把它们震出来。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But you may not have to go far to get this benefit.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但要获得这种好处，未必需要走很远。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Sometimes it's enough just to go for a walk. [ 16 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有时，只要出去散个步就够了。[16]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It also helps to travel in topic space.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在不同话题之间游历，也会有帮助。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You'll have more new ideas if you explore lots of different topics, partly because it gives the angle grinder more surface area to work on, and partly because analogies are an especially fruitful source of new ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 探索许多不同的话题，会带来更多新想法；一方面，这给了“角磨机”更大的工作表面；另一方面，类比是新想法特别丰富的来源。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Don't divide your attention evenly between many topics though, or you'll spread yourself too thin.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，不要把注意力 平均 分配给许多话题，那样你会过于分散。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You want to distribute it according to something more like a power law.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你应该按照一种更接近幂律的方式分配注意力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: [ 17 ] Be professionally curious about a few topics and idly curious about many more.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: [17]对少数话题保持专业层面的好奇，对更多话题保持随意的好奇。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Curiosity and originality are closely related.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 好奇心与原创性密切相关。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Curiosity feeds originality by giving it new things to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 好奇心通过提供新素材来滋养原创性。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But the relationship is closer than that.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但它们的关系比这更紧密。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Curiosity is itself a kind of originality; it's roughly to questions what originality is to answers.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 好奇心本身就是一种原创性；它对于问题的作用，就像原创性对于答案的作用。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And since questions at their best are a big component of answers, curiosity at its best is a creative force.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 既然最好的问题本身就是答案的重要组成部分，那么最好的好奇心本质上就是一种创造力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Having new ideas is a strange game, because it usually consists of seeing things that were right under your nose.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 获得新想法是一个奇怪的游戏，因为它通常意味着 看到那些就在你鼻子底下的东西。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Once you've seen a new idea, it tends to seem obvious.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一旦看到了新想法，它往往显得显而易见。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Why did no one think of this before?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 为什么以前没人想到呢？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When an idea seems simultaneously novel and obvious, it's probably a good one.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当一个想法既新颖又显而易见时，它很可能是个好想法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Seeing something obvious sounds easy.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 看见显而易见的东西，听起来很容易。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And yet empirically having new ideas is hard.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 然而，经验表明，产生新想法并不容易。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What's the source of this apparent contradiction?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这种表面上的矛盾，究竟从何而来？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It's that seeing the new idea usually requires you to change the way you look at the world.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 原因在于，发现新想法通常要求你改变看待世界的方式。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: We see the world through models that both help and constrain us.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我们通过模型来看世界，这些模型既帮助了我们，也限制了我们。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: When you fix a broken model, new ideas become obvious.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你修复了一个破碎的模型，新想法就会变得显而易见。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But noticing and fixing a broken model is hard.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但 发现并修复破碎的模型是很难的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's how new ideas can be both obvious and yet hard to discover: they're easy to see after you do something hard.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这就是为什么新想法既显而易见又难以发现：在你做了一件困难的事情（修复模型）之后，它们才变得容易看见。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One way to discover broken models is to be stricter than other people.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 发现破碎模型的一个方法是 比别人更严谨 （Stricter）。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Broken models of the world leave a trail of clues where they bash against reality.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 破碎的世界模型在与现实碰撞时会留下一串线索。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Most people don't want to see these clues.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 大多数人不想看到这些线索。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It would be an understatement to say that they're attached to their current model; it's what they think in; so they'll tend to ignore the trail of clues left by its breakage, however conspicuous it may seem in retrospect.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 说他们依恋现有模型都算是轻描淡写了；那是他们思考的依凭；所以他们倾向于忽略模型破裂留下的线索，无论事后看来这些线索有多么显眼。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: To find new ideas you have to seize on signs of breakage instead of looking away.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 要发现新想法，你必须 抓住这些破裂的迹象，而不是把视线移开。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: That's what Einstein did.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这就是爱因斯坦所做的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: He was able to see the wild implications of Maxwell's equations not so much because he was looking for new ideas as because he was stricter.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他能看到麦克斯韦方程组的疯狂含义，与其说是因为他在寻找新想法，不如说是因为他更严谨。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The other thing you need is a willingness to break rules.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你需要具备的另一种特质是 打破规则的意愿。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Paradoxical as it sounds, if you want to fix your model of the world, it helps to be the sort of person who's comfortable breaking rules.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这听起来很矛盾，但如果你想修复世界模型，最好做一个乐于打破规则的人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: From the point of view of the old model, which everyone including you initially shares, the new model usually breaks at least implicit rules.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 从旧模型的角度看（这也是包括你在内的所有人最初持有的观点），新模型通常打破了至少某些隐形规则。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Few understand the degree of rule-breaking required, because new ideas seem much more conservative once they succeed.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 很少有人明白，需要多大程度地打破规则，因为新想法一旦成功，看起来就会保守得多。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They seem perfectly reasonable once you're using the new model of the world they brought with them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 当你开始使用它们带来的新世界模型时，它们就显得完全合理了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But they didn't at the time; it took the greater part of a century for the heliocentric model to be generally accepted, even among astronomers, because it felt so wrong.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但在当时并非如此；日心说花了将近一个世纪才被普遍接受，甚至在天文学家中间也是如此，因为它当时感觉太“错”了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Indeed, if you think about it, a good new idea has to seem bad to most people, or someone would have already explored it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 事实上，如果你仔细想想，一个好的新想法必须在大多数人看来是“坏”的，否则早就有人去探索了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So what you're looking for is ideas that seem crazy, but the right kind of crazy.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 所以你要寻找的是那些 看起来疯狂，但疯狂得恰到好处的想法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: How do you recognize these?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 怎么辨别呢？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You can't with certainty.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你无法确切知道。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Often ideas that seem bad are bad.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 通常看起来坏的想法就是坏的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But ideas that are the right kind of crazy tend to be exciting; they're rich in implications; whereas ideas that are merely bad tend to be depressing.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但是，“好”的疯狂想法往往令人兴奋，充满潜在含义；而仅仅是“坏”的想法往往令人沮丧。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There are two ways to be comfortable breaking rules: to enjoy breaking them, and to be indifferent to them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 有两种方式可以让你从容地打破规则：一种是 享受 打破规则，一种是 漠视 规则。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: I call these two cases being aggressively and passively independent-minded.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我称之为“攻击性” （Aggressively）和 “被动性”（Passively）的独立思考。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The aggressively independent-minded are the naughty ones.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 攻击性的独立思考者 是淘气包。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Rules don't merely fail to stop them; breaking rules gives them additional energy.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 规则不仅无法阻止他们，打破规则反而给了他们额外的能量。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: For this sort of person, delight at the sheer audacity of a project sometimes supplies enough activation energy to get it started.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 对于这类人，仅仅是对项目“胆大包天”的喜悦，有时就足以提供启动所需的活化能。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The other way to break rules is not to care about them, or perhaps even to know they exist.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 另一种打破规则的方式是不在乎它们，甚至不知道它们的存在。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This is why novices and outsiders often make new discoveries; their ignorance of a field's assumptions acts as a source of temporary passive independent-mindedness.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这就是为什么 新手和局外人 经常会有新发现；他们对领域内既定假设的无知，成为了一种暂时的、被动的独立思考源泉。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Aspies also seem to have a kind of immunity to conventional beliefs.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 阿斯伯格综合征（Aspies）患者似乎也对传统观念有一种免疫力。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Several I know say that this helps them to have new ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 我认识好几个这样的人，他们说这对产生新想法很有帮助。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Strictness plus rule-breaking sounds like a strange combination.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 严谨 + 打破规则，这听起来像是一个奇怪的组合。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: In popular culture they're opposed.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在流行文化中，这两者是对立的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But popular culture has a broken model in this respect.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但这正是流行文化的模型破碎之处。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It implicitly assumes that issues are trivial ones, and in trivial matters strictness and rule-breaking are opposed.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它隐含地假设问题都是琐碎的；在琐碎的事情上，严谨和打破规则确实是对立的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But in questions that really matter, only rule-breakers can be truly strict.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但在真正重要的问题上，只有打破规则者才能做到真正的严谨。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: An overlooked idea often doesn't lose till the semifinals.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个被忽视的想法，往往直到半决赛才被淘汰。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You do see it, subconsciously, but then another part of your subconscious shoots it down because it would be too weird, too risky, too much work, too controversial.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你的潜意识其实看见了它，但潜意识的另一部分又把它否决了，因为它太古怪、太冒险、太费力，或太有争议。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: This suggests an exciting possibility: if you could turn off such filters, you could see more new ideas.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这暗示了一个令人兴奋的可能性：如果你能关掉这些潜意识过滤器，你就能看到更多新想法。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One way to do that is to ask what would be good ideas for someone else to explore.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个欺骗潜意识的方法是问自己：如果是别人来做，什么是一个好点子？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Then your subconscious won't shoot them down to protect you.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 这样你的潜意识就不会为了保护你而枪毙它。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: You could also discover overlooked ideas by working in the other direction: by starting from what's obscuring them.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 你也可以反向寻找被忽视的想法：从遮蔽它们的东西入手。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Every cherished but mistaken principle is surrounded by a dead zone of valuable ideas that are unexplored because they contradict it.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 每一个受到珍视却错误的原则周围，都有一片有价值想法的空白地带；只因这些想法与它矛盾，就一直无人探索。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Religions are collections of cherished but mistaken principles.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 宗教 就是这类原则的集合。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So anything that can be described either literally or metaphorically as a religion will have valuable unexplored ideas in its shadow.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 任何可以被字面上或隐喻上称为“宗教”的东西，在其阴影下都藏着未被挖掘的宝藏。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Copernicus and Darwin both made discoveries of this type. [ 18 ]
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 哥白尼和达尔文都做出了这类发现。[18]

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What are people in your field religious about, in the sense of being too attached to some principle that might not be as self-evident as they think?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在你所处的领域，人们对什么东西持有“宗教般”的执念？有什么原则是他们深信不疑，但其实并非不证自明的？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: What becomes possible if you discard it?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你抛弃它，会有什么新的可能？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: People show much more originality in solving problems than in deciding which problems to solve.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 人们在 解决问题 时表现出的原创性，远超在 决定解决什么问题 时。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Even the smartest can be surprisingly conservative when deciding what to work on.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 即使是最聪明的人，在选题时也保守得惊人。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: People who'd never dream of being fashionable in any other way get sucked into working on fashionable problems.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 那些在其他方面绝不随大流的人，却常常被吸进“时髦问题”的黑洞。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One reason people are more conservative when choosing problems than solutions is that problems are bigger bets.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 人们在选题上保守，部分是因为 问题是更大的赌注。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: A problem could occupy you for years, while exploring a solution might only take days.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 一个问题可能占据你数年光阴，而探索一个解决方案可能只需几天。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But even so I think most people are too conservative.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 但即便如此，大多数人还是太保守了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: They're not merely responding to risk, but to fashion as well.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 他们不仅是在规避风险，更是在追逐时尚。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Unfashionable problems are undervalued.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不时髦的问题被严重低估了。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: One of the most interesting kinds of unfashionable problem is the problem that people think has been fully explored, but hasn't.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 最有趣的一种不时髦问题是：那些人们以为已经被研究透了，其实并没有的问题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Great work often takes something that already exists and shows its latent potential.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 伟大的工作往往是发掘既有事物的潜在价值。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Durer and Watt both did this.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 丢勒（Durer）和瓦特（Watt）都是如此。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: So if you're interested in a field that others think is tapped out, don't let their skepticism deter you.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如果你对某个别人认为已经“枯竭”的领域感兴趣，别让他们的怀疑劝退你。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: People are often wrong about this.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 在这件事上，大家通常是错的。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Working on an unfashionable problem can be very pleasing.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 研究不时髦的问题是一种愉悦的体验。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: There's no hype or hurry.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 没有炒作，没有匆忙。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: Opportunists and critics are both occupied elsewhere.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 投机者和批评家都忙着去别处凑热闹。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: The existing work often has an old-school solidity.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 现有的工作往往带有一种老派的坚实感。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: And there's a satisfying sense of economy in cultivating ideas that would otherwise be wasted.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 而且，利用那些本会被浪费的想法，会给你一种令人满足的“经济感”。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: But the most common type of overlooked problem is not explicitly unfashionable in the sense of being out of fashion.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 不过，最常见的被忽视的问题，并不是那种明显已经过时的问题。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: It just doesn't seem to matter as much as it actually does.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 它只是 看起来没那么重要。

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: How do you find these?
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 如何找到它们？

gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.en: By being self-indulgent — by letting your curiosity have its way, and tuning out, at least temporarily, the little voice in your head that says you should only be working on "important" problems.
gr-pg-how-to-do-great-work.cn: 做一个自我放纵的人 ——让你的好奇心做主，暂时屏蔽脑子里那个告诉你只做“重要”工作的声音。
